items.title: NEW: ProPublica revealed that the FBI was circling Sen. Collins over a defense contractor’s donations — until Trump gutt
NEW: ProPublica revealed that the FBI was circling Sen. Collins over a defense contractor’s donations — until Trump g…
YOU CAN SEE EVERYTHING Trailer (2026) Elizabeth Holmes

editorial.brief: Two stories crossed feeds today: Bluesky and Mastodon both carried ProPublica's report tying an FBI look at Senator Collins to a defense contractor's donations, and Elizabeth Holmes turned up on both Wikipedia and YouTube. Neither beat the day's single biggest number: Lizzie Borden drew 586,575 Wikipedia views, more than triple anyone else on the list, for reasons the data doesn't supply.
editorial.cover_sub: A nineteenth-century murder case outdrew Elizabeth Holmes, an Asian Games, and a serial killer's Wikipedia page combined, with nothing in today's feeds explaining why.
editorial.wiki_deck: Lizzie Borden led every other Wikipedia article by more than three to one today, and nothing in the day's news, trends, or social chatter accounts for it.
editorial.letter_headline: One old case outran everything new
editorial.discourse_deck: Hacker News is heads-down on AI and hardware, Lemmy is sardonic about capitalism and bureaucracy, Bluesky is split between breaking political reporting and idle amusement, and Mastodon is watching bugs and marmots.
editorial.foreign_deck: The AI wire covered Oracle's 97.9 percent chip utilization and Anthropic's own chief urging a slower pace, while search interest ran to the Dodgers in the US, share prices in India, and a cyclone.
editorial.markets_deck: Baseball dominates by volume, with Padres-Dodgers trading at 100 percent yes on a million dollars, while a geopolitical question on Kharg Island sits frozen at zero.
editorial.watch_deck: Counter-Strike 2 held 1,452,036 concurrent players tonight, well ahead of Dota 2's 805,725 and PUBG's 731,479, with Padres-Dodgers and Astros-Mariners drawing the bettors' money.
editorial.yt_headline: An A24 trailer, not a song
editorial.yt_note: You Can See Everything led the trending list with 3,372,795 views, ahead of a reaction video, a Knights of Guinevere episode trailer, and two music videos trailing well behind.
editorial.closing_note: By tomorrow's edition, Lizzie Borden's spike will likely have receded, the Lemmy post titled Wow! will have been replaced by some other one-word verdict, and the Kharg Island market will either have resolved or kept sitting at zero. The FBI-Collins story is the one worth watching for whether it grows.
wiki_paras: Lizzie Borden topped Wikipedia's most-read list with 586,575 views, ahead of Elizabeth Holmes at 184,994, the 2026 Asian Games at 163,446, Aileen Wuornos at 160,292, and musician Angry Anderson at 151,152. Three of the five slots belong to figures tied to violent crime.

The margin was 3.2 times the runner-up, a gap wide enough to suggest a single cause rather than background curiosity. Elizabeth Holmes had help explaining her showing, appearing on YouTube as well as Wikipedia. Borden had no such company anywhere else in today's feeds.

No documentary premiere, anniversary, or news item in this snapshot points to a trigger. That itself is the finding: on a day with no breaking Borden story visible anywhere else, the internet still sent well over half a million people to read about her.
letter_paras: Today's snapshot has a lopsided shape. Wikipedia produced a runaway winner in Lizzie Borden, at more than three times her nearest competitor, while everywhere else the internet stayed scattered: Lemmy voted up a post titled simply Wow!, Hacker News split between chip news and enzyme research, and the social feeds drifted through weather, marmots, and one shared political story.

The smaller corners told their own story. Product Hunt's top two entries, tiun. and CREEM 2.0, finished five votes apart. USGS logged 25 earthquakes above magnitude 2.5 in the last day, the largest a 5.7 near Tonga that will register on no dashboard but its own. A Hacker News post about a transputer C compiler sat at 16 points, unbothered by any of it.

A same-hour snapshot doesn't explain why Lizzie Borden won today, and that gap is the point. Most days settle into a tidy story by the time anyone writes about them; catching every feed at once, before the internet has agreed on a narrative, preserves the version where a 132-year-old case can outperform Wikipedia's arguments and appear to owe nothing to anything currently happening.

brief: Two stories crossed feeds today: Bluesky and Mastodon both carried ProPublica's report tying an FBI look at Senator Collins to a defense contractor's donations, and Elizabeth Holmes turned up on both Wikipedia and YouTube. Neither beat the day's single biggest number: Lizzie Borden drew 586,575 Wikipedia views, more than triple anyone else on the list, for reasons the data doesn't supply.
